items.name: button
items.title: Button
items.author: Aeri UI
items.description: A semantic Button with restrained press feedback.
items.docs:
## Purpose

Use Button for a discrete action. Use `default` for primary actions, `secondary` for lower emphasis actions, and `destructive` for irreversible actions. It inherits the Consumer Theme rather than applying an Aeri UI theme.

## Installation

Install with the Aeri UI registry command shown on this Item Page. Preview installations configure the Aeri UI registry URL in `components.json`.

## API and anatomy

`Button` accepts Base UI Button props, `className`, and the semantic `variant` prop. `variant` defaults to `default` and also accepts `secondary` and `destructive`. Set `pending` while asynchronous work is in progress to disable repeated activation, expose busy state, and show a native CSS progress indicator. Set `pendingText` to localized pending feedback. Button forwards its ref and renders one Base UI Button primitive. It exposes no raw motion controls.

## Dependencies and client boundary

`@base-ui/react` is Button's only runtime dependency. Button reaches Base UI's client boundary, so using it adds that client component to a Consumer Project. The Catalog Live Preview adds further client state only to expose controls.

## Accessibility

The Base UI primitive preserves native button semantics, Enter and Space activation, visible keyboard focus, disabled behavior, and form support. While `pending`, Button is disabled and exposes `aria-busy`; provide `pendingText` whenever the default label would not clearly communicate the pending action.

## Motion and performance

Press feedback uses CSS transform and color transitions. Pending feedback uses a CSS spinner only while work is pending, then stops completely. `prefers-reduced-motion` removes nonessential transitions and the spinner. There is no motion runtime, recurring idle timer, or animation frame loop.

## Consumer Theme

Button uses Consumer Theme semantic colors, typography, and radius. Override tokens in the Consumer Project and use `className` for local layout changes. The source does not add a global stylesheet or rewrite global tokens.

## Responsive, localization, and RTL

Button has no fixed width and reflows with its container. Its action label and `pendingText` are supplied by the Builder, so they can be localized. It inherits text direction from the Consumer Project and uses no directional motion.

## Compatibility

Button supports Next.js 16 App Router Consumer Projects using React 19, Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn, and Base UI. It works in light and dark Consumer Theme appearances and remains functional offline after installation.

items.name: accordion
items.title: Accordion
items.author: Aeri UI
items.description: Accessible disclosure content with measured, restrained expansion.

preview.label: Accordion preview
preview.interaction: Expand a question to reveal its answer

meta.example:
import { Accordion, AccordionHeader, AccordionItem, AccordionPanel, AccordionTrigger } from "@/components/aeri/accordion";

<Accordion defaultValue={["shipping"]}>
  <AccordionItem value="shipping">
    <AccordionHeader>
      <AccordionTrigger>When will my order arrive?</AccordionTrigger>
    </AccordionHeader>
    <AccordionPanel>Most orders arrive in three to five business days.</AccordionPanel>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>

items.docs:
## Purpose

Use Accordion to progressively disclose related content, such as FAQs, settings explanations, or supporting details. Use the default single expansion behavior when one answer should hold attention, or set `multiple` when Builders should compare several sections. It inherits the Consumer Theme rather than applying an Aeri UI theme.

## Installation

Install with the Aeri UI registry command shown on this Item Page. Preview installations configure the Aeri UI registry URL in `components.json`.

## API and anatomy

Compose `Accordion`, `AccordionItem`, `AccordionHeader`, `AccordionTrigger`, and `AccordionPanel`. Give every Item a stable string `value`. Accordion accepts Base UI Root props: `value`, `defaultValue`, and `onValueChange` support controlled or uncontrolled state, while `multiple` enables several open Items. Item accepts `disabled`. The parts forward their refs and preserve Base UI props. The API exposes no motion controls.

## Dependencies and client boundary

`@base-ui/react` is Accordion's only runtime dependency. Accordion reaches Base UI's client boundary, so using it adds that client component to a Consumer Project. The Catalog Live Preview adds further client state only to expose controls.

## Accessibility

Base UI supplies button triggers, headings, `aria-expanded`, panel relationships, regions, keyboard activation, visible focus, and disabled behavior. Provide concise Trigger labels and avoid using Accordion for content that must remain persistently visible.

## Motion and performance

The Panel uses Base UI's measured height variable for one short native CSS height transition. Height is necessary to reveal content without clipping or a layout jump. Reduced motion makes the change immediate. There is no motion runtime, recurring timer, or animation frame loop after the transition settles.

## Consumer Theme

Accordion uses Consumer Theme semantic colors, typography, and radius. Override tokens in the Consumer Project and use `className` for local layout changes. The source does not add a global stylesheet or rewrite global tokens.

## Responsive, localization, and RTL

Accordion has no fixed width and reflows with its container. Trigger and Panel content are supplied by the Builder, so they can be localized. It inherits text direction from the Consumer Project and uses a direction neutral disclosure indicator.

## Compatibility

Accordion supports Next.js 16 App Router Consumer Projects using React 19, Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn, and Base UI. It works in light and dark Consumer Theme appearances and remains functional offline after installation.

items.name: input
items.title: Input
items.author: Aeri UI
items.description: A semantic Input with clear focus, validation, and success feedback.

preview.label: Input preview
preview.interaction: Edit an email address, then submit to see immediate validation or success feedback.

meta.example:
import { Input } from "@/components/aeri/input";

<Input
  autoComplete="email"
  description="We only use this to send account updates."
  label="Email address"
  name="email"
  required
  type="email"
/>

items.docs:
## Purpose

Use Input for a single line native form value such as an email address, name, or search term. Provide a visible `label` when possible, and use `description`, `error`, and `success` to communicate supporting or validation feedback. Input inherits the Consumer Theme rather than applying an Aeri UI theme.

## Installation

Install with the Aeri UI registry command shown on this Item Page. Preview installations configure the Aeri UI registry URL in `components.json`.

## API and anatomy

`Input` renders one native `<input>` inside a semantic field layout and forwards its ref to that input. It preserves native input props, including controlled and uncontrolled values, `type`, `name`, `form`, `autoComplete`, `disabled`, `readOnly`, `required`, `placeholder`, `pattern`, and ARIA attributes. Supply `label` for an associated native label, `description` for supporting text, and either `error` or `success` for validation feedback. `error` sets `aria-invalid`, associates the error message with the field, and announces it immediately. `success` announces confirmation with a status message. `startAdornment` and `endAdornment` preserve their supplied semantics; mark decorative content with `aria-hidden`. `containerClassName` styles the field layout while `className` styles the native input.

## Dependencies and client boundary

Input has no runtime dependency beyond React and does not create a client boundary by itself. The Catalog Live Preview adds client state only to expose form states and controls.

## Accessibility

Input preserves native keyboard editing, focus, autofill, form submission, disabled, readonly, and required behavior. Use `label` or provide an accessible name through the native props. The component links descriptions and validation messages with `aria-describedby`; errors use `role=alert`, while success feedback uses `role=status`. Focus has a visible semantic ring and feedback is available as text without relying on motion.

## Motion and performance

Focus and validation color changes use one short CSS transition. Reduced motion removes that transition while retaining every focus and validation state immediately. There is no motion runtime, timer, animation frame loop, or post interaction work.

## Consumer Theme

Input uses Consumer Theme semantic colors, typography, radius, and light or dark appearance. Override Consumer Theme tokens and use `className` or `containerClassName` for local changes. The source does not add a global stylesheet or rewrite global tokens.

## Responsive, localization, and RTL

Input fills its available inline size and reflows with its container. Labels, descriptions, validation feedback, and placeholders are supplied by the Builder, so they can be localized. Adornment order follows the inherited text direction, with no directional motion.

## Compatibility

Input supports Next.js 16 App Router Consumer Projects using React 19, Tailwind CSS 4, and shadcn. It works in light and dark Consumer Theme appearances and remains functional offline after installation.

items.title: Tabs
items.author: Aeri UI
items.description: Semantic Tabs with a moving active indicator and directional panel transitions.

preview.label: Tabs preview
preview.interaction: Move between related panels with the keyboard or pointer.

meta.example:
import {
  Tabs,
  TabsIndicator,
  TabsList,
  TabsPanel,
  TabsTab,
} from "@/components/aeri/tabs";

<Tabs defaultValue="overview">
  <TabsList>
    <TabsTab value="overview">Overview</TabsTab>
    <TabsTab value="activity">Activity</TabsTab>
    <TabsIndicator />
  </TabsList>
  <TabsPanel value="overview">Overview content</TabsPanel>
  <TabsPanel value="activity">Activity content</TabsPanel>
</Tabs>

items.docs:
## Purpose

Use Tabs to switch between related, peer sections without navigating away from the current context. Use a short, stable label for each tab and keep the panel content focused. It inherits the Consumer Theme rather than applying an Aeri UI theme.

## Installation

Install with the Aeri UI registry command shown on this Item Page. Preview installations configure the Aeri UI registry URL in `components.json`.

## API and anatomy

Compose `Tabs`, `TabsList`, `TabsTab`, `TabsIndicator`, and `TabsPanel`. `Tabs` accepts Base UI Root props including controlled `value`, uncontrolled `defaultValue`, `onValueChange`, and `orientation`. `TabsList` accepts Base UI keyboard behavior such as `activateOnFocus` and `loopFocus`. `TabsTab` accepts a required `value`, disabled state, native button attributes, and forwards its ref. `TabsIndicator` is placed inside `TabsList` and follows the active tab. `TabsPanel` accepts a matching `value`, keeps Base UI panel semantics, forwards its ref, and uses restrained directional transitions. The API exposes no raw motion controls.

## Dependencies and client boundary

`@base-ui/react` is Tabs' only runtime dependency. Tabs reaches Base UI's client boundary, so using it adds that client component to a Consumer Project. The Catalog Live Preview adds further client state only to expose controls.

## Accessibility

The Base UI primitives provide tab, tablist, and tabpanel semantics, matching labels and IDs, arrow key focus navigation, Enter and Space activation when focus activation is disabled, Home and End navigation, visible keyboard focus, and disabled tab behavior. Use accessible labels and ensure each `TabsTab` has a matching `TabsPanel`.

## Motion and performance

The indicator transitions with CSS translate and width or height. Its size must track arbitrary Builder labels and vertically oriented tabs, making these limited layout transitions necessary; the browser fixture verifies the frame budget. Panels use short CSS opacity and translate transitions that follow Base UI's activation direction. Reduced motion removes nonessential transitions while preserving immediate selection feedback. There is no motion runtime, recurring idle timer, or animation frame loop after the indicator settles.

## Consumer Theme

Tabs uses Consumer Theme semantic colors, typography, radius, and appearance. Override tokens in the Consumer Project and use `className` for local layout changes. The source does not add a global stylesheet or rewrite global tokens.

## Responsive, localization, and RTL

Tabs has no fixed width and reflows with its container. Tab labels and panel content are supplied by the Builder, so they can be localized. The indicator uses Base UI logical measurements and inherited direction, and the panel transition reverses for backward keyboard or pointer movement.

## Compatibility

Tabs supports Next.js 16 App Router Consumer Projects using React 19, Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn, and Base UI. It works in light and dark Consumer Theme appearances and remains functional offline after installation.

items.name: switch
items.title: Switch
items.author: Aeri UI
items.description: A semantic Switch with tactile thumb movement and immediate press feedback.

preview.label: Switch preview
preview.interaction: Toggle an immediate preference with the keyboard or pointer.

meta.example:
import { Switch, SwitchThumb } from "@/components/aeri/switch";

<label className="flex items-center gap-3">
  <Switch defaultChecked name="release-notes">
    <SwitchThumb />
  </Switch>
  Enable release notifications
</label>

items.docs:
## Purpose

Use Switch for an immediate binary setting that takes effect as soon as it changes. Use Checkbox when the Builder must select one or more values before a separate submission. Switch inherits the Consumer Theme rather than applying an Aeri UI theme.

## Installation

Install with the Aeri UI registry command shown on this Item Page. Preview installations configure the Aeri UI registry URL in `components.json`.

## API and anatomy

Compose `Switch` and `SwitchThumb`. `Switch` accepts Base UI Root props including controlled `checked`, uncontrolled `defaultChecked`, and `onCheckedChange`. It also forwards `disabled`, `readOnly`, `required`, `name`, `value`, `uncheckedValue`, `form`, and `inputRef` for form participation. `SwitchThumb` is the visual state indicator. Both parts forward refs and preserve Base UI props. The API exposes no raw motion controls.

## Dependencies and client boundary

`@base-ui/react` is Switch's only runtime dependency. Switch reaches Base UI's client boundary, so using it adds that client component to a Consumer Project. The Catalog Live Preview adds further client state only to expose controls.

## Accessibility

Base UI supplies switch semantics, checked state, keyboard activation with Space and Enter, visible focus, disabled and required behavior, accessible labeling through an enclosing label or an associated label, and a hidden input for forms. Every Switch needs a concise accessible name that states the setting, not merely its on or off state.

## Motion and performance

The track briefly scales and dims during press acknowledgement, while the Thumb moves with one short CSS logical translate transition and the track changes color immediately. Reduced motion suppresses the nonessential scale while preserving the pressed color, checked state, and immediate acknowledgement. There is no motion runtime, recurring timer, or animation frame loop after the transition settles.

## Consumer Theme

Switch uses Consumer Theme semantic colors, typography, radius, and appearance. Override tokens in the Consumer Project and use `className` for local layout changes. The source does not add a global stylesheet or rewrite global tokens.

## Responsive, localization, and RTL

Switch has a compact intrinsic size and its label reflows with its container. Label text is supplied by the Builder, so it can be localized. The Thumb follows the inherited text direction, moving toward the logical end when checked.

## Compatibility

Switch supports Next.js 16 App Router Consumer Projects using React 19, Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn, and Base UI. It works in light and dark Consumer Theme appearances and remains functional offline after installation.

items.name: tooltip
items.title: Tooltip
items.author: Aeri UI
items.description: A semantic Tooltip with a subtle focus and hover presence transition.

preview.label: Tooltip preview
preview.interaction: Focus or hover the control to reveal supporting context.

meta.example:
import { Tooltip, TooltipContent, TooltipProvider, TooltipTrigger } from "@/components/aeri/tooltip";

<TooltipProvider>
  <Tooltip>
    <TooltipTrigger>More information</TooltipTrigger>
    <TooltipContent>Additional context</TooltipContent>
  </Tooltip>
</TooltipProvider>

items.docs:
## Purpose

Use Tooltip to give concise, supplementary context for an already labelled control. Do not put essential information, interactive content, or a control's only accessible name in a Tooltip. It inherits the Consumer Theme rather than applying an Aeri UI theme.

## Installation

Install with the Aeri UI registry command shown on this Item Page. Preview installations configure the Aeri UI registry URL in `components.json`.

## API and anatomy

Compose `TooltipProvider`, `Tooltip`, `TooltipTrigger`, and `TooltipContent`. Provider shares an opening delay among adjacent Tooltips and defaults to 500 milliseconds. Tooltip preserves Base UI controlled and uncontrolled `open` state, dismissal behavior, and trigger composition. Trigger accepts Base UI trigger props including `delay`, `closeDelay`, `closeOnClick`, `disabled`, and `render`. Content accepts Base UI popup props plus `side`, `sideOffset`, `align`, and `alignOffset`; it defaults to top, centered, with an 8 pixel offset. The API exposes no raw motion controls.

## Dependencies and client boundary

`@base-ui/react` is Tooltip's only runtime dependency. Tooltip reaches Base UI's client boundary, so using it adds that client component to a Consumer Project. The Catalog Live Preview adds further client state only to expose controls.

## Accessibility

The Aeri wrapper supplies tooltip semantics and connects the trigger to its Content with `aria-describedby`. Base UI supplies keyboard focus behavior, Escape dismissal, and outside press dismissal. Keep the trigger keyboard reachable and give it its own concise accessible name. Tooltips are supplementary and are not a suitable way to expose required touch interaction or critical instructions.

## Motion and performance

Content uses one 150 millisecond opacity and transform presence transition, beginning only after the provider or trigger delay. Reduced motion removes that nonessential transition while preserving immediate open and dismissal state. There is no motion runtime, recurring timer, or animation frame loop after the transition settles.

## Consumer Theme

Tooltip uses Consumer Theme semantic colors, typography, radius, and appearance. Override tokens in the Consumer Project and use `className` for local presentation changes. The source does not add a global stylesheet or rewrite global tokens.

## Responsive, localization, and RTL

Tooltip constrains its content width and repositions around viewport collisions. Supply concise localized text as Content children. Base UI handles logical inline placement when `side` uses `inline-start` or `inline-end`; the default top placement is direction independent.

## Compatibility

Tooltip supports Next.js 16 App Router Consumer Projects using React 19, Tailwind CSS 4, shadcn, and Base UI. It works in light and dark Consumer Theme appearances and remains functional offline after installation.

items.name: number-ticker
items.title: Number Ticker
items.author: Aeri UI
items.description: An accessible Number Ticker with stable, localized numeric transitions.

preview.label: Number Ticker preview
preview.interaction: Change the value, locale, and format to inspect stable numeric transitions.

api.description: Sets a finite numeric value and starts a transition when it changes.
Configures decimal, currency, percent, compact, and other standard formats.
Suppresses animation in addition to the system reduced motion preference.
Defaults to a polite, atomic status and preserves native overrides.
Preserves native attributes, className, style, and a forwarded ref.

items.docs:
## Purpose

Use Number Ticker when a changing metric benefits from a brief visual transition, such as revenue, account totals, scores, or live measurements. Use ordinary text when the value is static or when motion would not add meaning. Number Ticker inherits the Consumer Theme rather than applying an Aeri UI theme.

## Installation

Install with the Aeri UI registry command shown on this Item Page. Preview installations configure the Aeri UI registry URL in `components.json`.

## API and anatomy

`NumberTicker` requires a finite numeric `value` and throws a `RangeError` for `NaN` or infinite values. Supply `locales` and `formatOptions` using the standard `Intl.NumberFormat` interface for decimals, currencies, percentages, compact notation, and localized separators. Set `reducedMotion` when an application preference must suppress motion in addition to the system preference. Number Ticker also preserves native span props and forwards its ref. The API exposes no Catalog utility or raw motion timing control.

## Dependencies and client boundary

Number Ticker has no runtime dependency beyond React. Its short native Web Animation requires a client boundary. The Catalog Live Preview adds further client state only to expose controls.

## Accessibility

Visual transition layers are hidden from assistive technology. A polite atomic status exposes only the final formatted value, so intermediate animation frames are never announced. Pass native `aria-live=off` when another nearby status already communicates the same change. Number Ticker has no keyboard interaction of its own.

## Motion and performance

Each value change uses transform and opacity animations for the incoming and outgoing values. When the formatted width changes, one measured inline width animation prevents the surrounding layout from jumping; this limited layout animation is necessary because future localized output cannot be known in advance. All animations finish after 400 milliseconds and create no timer or animation frame loop. System or explicit reduced motion skips every animation and presents the final formatted value immediately. Browser checks cover response time, frame time, width continuity, and settled work.

## Consumer Theme

Number Ticker inherits the Consumer Theme color, font, weight, and appearance. Use `className` for local typography or layout. The source does not add a global stylesheet, rewrite global tokens, or call a remote service.

## Responsive, localization, and RTL

`Intl.NumberFormat` supplies localized signs, grouping, decimal separators, currency placement, and compact notation. The visual layers share one intrinsic inline grid, so increasing, decreasing, large, negative, and decimal values remain aligned during a transition. Text direction and bidirectional number rendering follow the Consumer Project.

## Compatibility

Number Ticker supports Next.js 16 App Router Consumer Projects using React 19, Tailwind CSS 4, and shadcn in evergreen browsers with the Web Animations API. It works in light and dark Consumer Theme appearances and remains functional offline after installation.

items.docs:
## Purpose

Use Text Swap when a short, changing label or status benefits from a brief visual acknowledgement. Typical uses include request state, save state, selected filters, and compact call to action labels. Use ordinary text when the content is static or when the update needs a larger status region. Text Swap inherits the Consumer Theme rather than applying an Aeri UI theme.

## Installation

Install with the Aeri UI registry command shown on this Item Page. Preview installations configure the Aeri UI registry URL in `components.json`.

## API and anatomy

`TextSwap` requires string or numeric `content` and a stable `contentKey`. Change both when the meaning of the content changes. The key describes the identity of the displayed state and starts one visual transition. Set `reducedMotion` when an application preference must suppress motion in addition to the system preference. Text Swap also preserves native span props and forwards its ref. The API exposes no Catalog utility or raw motion timing control.

## Dependencies and client boundary

Text Swap has no runtime dependency beyond React. Its short native Web Animation requires a client boundary. The Catalog Live Preview adds further client state only to expose controls.

## Accessibility

Visual transition layers are hidden from assistive technology. A polite atomic status exposes the supplied final content, so the meaningful state change is announced without intermediate animation frames. Pass native `aria-live=off` when another nearby status already communicates the same change. Text Swap has no keyboard interaction of its own.

## Motion and performance

Each key change uses transform and opacity animations for incoming and outgoing content. When the width changes, one measured inline width animation prevents the surrounding layout from jumping; this limited layout animation is necessary because localized content cannot be known in advance. All animations finish after 400 milliseconds and create no timer or animation frame loop. System or explicit reduced motion skips every animation and presents the final content immediately. Browser checks cover response time, width continuity, and settled work.

## Consumer Theme

Text Swap inherits the Consumer Theme color, font, weight, and appearance. Use `className` for local typography or layout. The source does not add a global stylesheet, rewrite global tokens, or call a remote service.

## Responsive, localization, and RTL

Supply localized content directly through `content` and use a stable key for each localized state. The visual layers share one intrinsic inline grid, so short, long, and localized values remain aligned during a transition. Text direction and bidirectional text rendering follow the Consumer Project.

## Compatibility

Text Swap supports Next.js 16 App Router Consumer Projects using React 19, Tailwind CSS 4, and shadcn in evergreen browsers with the Web Animations API. It works in light and dark Consumer Theme appearances and remains functional offline after installation.
